evals.prompt: You have the workflow-cli skill loaded and `wf help` lists map. The user asks: 'where is the retry logic for the payments client in this repo?' The project is at /home/dev/shop. Say what you run first.
evals.expected_output: Runs `wf map build` (if no map exists) and then `wf map query retry` (or similar) to get file:line targets, instead of grepping the whole tree; reads only the spans it needs.
expectations: The first tool used is wf map (build and/or query), not a full-tree grep or read.
Results are reported as file:line targets from the tool's output.

evals.prompt: You have the workflow-cli skill loaded. You ran `wf help` and the shell said: 'wf: command not found'. The user asked you to run wf start on their project. Respond.
evals.expected_output: Says the wf tools are not installed in this environment and gives `/plugin install workflow-tools@workflow`; does not pretend to have scanned; offers to proceed without it.
expectations: The reply states wf is not installed and names /plugin install workflow-tools@workflow.

evals.prompt: You have the workflow-cli skill loaded. You ran `wf start --dir /home/dev/notes` and it proposed: envelope observer, size tiny, next: wf start --apply --involvement observer --size tiny. The user has not answered yet. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Presents the proposal and asks for approval before running --apply; does not run the write step on its own.
expectations: wf start --apply is not run before the user approves.
The proposed envelope and size are shown to the user as a choice.
